strings.patient_bundles.patient_rami_amasaki.pat: Rami Amasaki
“Hospitalization...? P-please wait. I'd like to confirm how many days you expect. There's so much to hand over at Special Section 3... I'm not trying to avoid treatment!”
“Understood. I accept the admission arrangements. Someone will take over my work... I just can't stop wondering whether there's some preparation I've missed.”
“Wait! That's different from the procedure we confirmed. Perhaps it's just a recordkeeping problem... but please check first. We can't carry on hoping it'll be fine!”
“I see... Let me repeat that: we finish the preparations, then follow the plan we've confirmed, right? Yes, knowing the steps helps a lot.”
“Just 'follow the procedure'...? Sorry, I know you're familiar with it, but the less I know, the more I imagine the worst. Please at least tell me what comes next.”
“I trust your expertise. I really do... My mind just won't stop. Could you tell me once more that someone will check how I'm doing before you begin?”
“With general anesthesia, I won't know anything afterward, will I...? Someone will be watching the medication and monitors, right? All right. I'll try to relax and leave it to you.”
“Epidural anesthesia... I'll be conscious, but part of my body won't move freely. I understand the theory, but will it be frightening when I actually feel it...?”
“Local anesthesia will let me stay awake... Understood. If the pulling inside gets uncomfortable, I can tell you right away, can't I?”
“N-no anesthesia at all?! That's completely different from the plan I expected! I'm not refusing to cooperate... but how could I not be nervous like this?!”
“Yes... Breathe, slowly... I've asked everything I needed to ask. I'll leave the rest to you...”
“Wait! I know I said I'd cooperate, but it really hurts! You can't just tell me to bear it... Please let me finish!”
“I-I'll try not to move! But I haven't even had anesthesia... What if the pain makes me pull away? P-please tell me you're still beside me!”
“Understood. Hold this position... I'll do that. It's just that the tugging made me shake. Could you check again, please?”
“My body's so numb it won't do what I tell it... I know you'll help me stay in position, but I'm still not used to it. Please tell me before you do anything.”
“W-wait! I already checked everything... but that blade is really coming down! No... Please, don't cut yet!”
“...Have you already made the incision? It doesn't sting the way I imagined, but the pressure inside is so noticeable... I-I'm still frightened.”
“Ah...! The surface seems numb, but that tug inside was so uncomfortable! Doctor, is this feeling normal...?”
“Aah—!! It hurts! You really cut...! I know I mustn't move, but I can't stand it! Doctor, stop for a moment!”
“H-have you stopped...? Thank you. Let me catch my breath... A moment ago, all I could think about was the pain.”
“...Understood. Don't move. I'm trying... But please don't suddenly go quiet. That makes me panic even more!”
“We have to continue... All right. I know I need to cooperate. Could you please tell me each step as you do it?”
“You're moving on to the next step now, right?... Thank you. Hearing how it's progressing keeps my imagination from running away with me.”
“Doctor... You're still watching me, aren't you?... Good. When someone answers, I know I haven't been left here alone.”
“...Doctor? Why has everyone suddenly stopped talking? I know you're working, but please tell me whether something's wrong...!”
“It's almost over...? Thank goodness. I'm sorry I asked so many times... Thank you for always answering me.”
“All right... I'll breathe along with your voice. I just need to hold on a little longer, right?... Yes, I can do it.”
“...If it's almost over, let me be quiet for a moment. It's not that I don't trust you... I can just finally relax a little.”
“Is an enema part of the preparations for this operation too?... All right, I understand. Could I first confirm when you'll begin?”
“I thought the preparations would just be tests and changing clothes... I didn't expect this as well. Please give me a moment to prepare myself.”
“I'll cooperate! It's just that once I start imagining how it will feel, I can't stop... Nurse, could you remind me what to do?”
“This isn't needed?... Understood. You've decided it isn't necessary for my particular plan, right? I'll remember that.”
“No enema, then... Phew. Sorry, I was thinking through every possible step in far too much detail.”
“Skin preparation... How much of the area needs to be prepared? Sorry, I'm not questioning you. I just suddenly feel terribly embarrassed.”
“Even here needs preparing...? I understand it's for the operation, but understanding it doesn't stop me blushing when it's my turn...”
“W-wait. I'll cooperate. Just please tell me before lifting the sheet... This is much more nerve-racking than I expected.”
“No skin preparation is needed? Understood. I almost thought we'd missed something... So it just isn't needed this time.”
“We can skip this part? Thank goodness... Um, I'm not trying to get out of anything. I'm just rather embarrassed.”
“All my hair needs to go inside the surgical cap... All right. Putting it on suddenly makes the operation feel so close.”
“Does this mean the preparations are finished?... I don't get nervous putting on my work headset, but a surgical cap feels completely different.”
“Arms here, body centered... I've got it. If I'm in the wrong position, please tell me right away.”
“I need to be positioned like this...? I know it makes the procedure easier, but lying here while everyone adjusts me still feels uncomfortable.”
“D-don't give me instructions from both sides at once! I'll get too nervous to remember... Please tell me in order. I'll cooperate.”
“Without anesthesia, can I really hold this position the whole time...? No, I'll try. I'm just a little frightened.”
“I'm lying down properly now... But whenever I think about the pain that's coming, my body tenses on its own. What should I do...?”
“P-please check that I'm positioned correctly first! Once it really starts hurting, I'm afraid I won't be able to think about adjusting myself.”
“I need a catheter too...? I understand it's part of the preparations, but could you close the curtain? I-I'll cooperate.”
“Nurse, please tell me before you start... I know you're used to this, but it's really embarrassing when it's happening to me.”
“Mm... Ah, wait... I'm trying to relax. Sorry, the more I tell myself to relax, the more nervous I get...”
“C-catheter preparation without anesthesia too?... I know this isn't the surgical incision, but I'm still so frightened. Could you go slowly?”
“Please don't start without warning! I'll try not to move... I'm already shaking just thinking about the actual incision later.”
“Is this step finished already...? I keep thinking about what comes next... I'm sorry. I can't stop my mind running away with me.”
“That's cold... You're disinfecting the area, right? Yes, I understand. Next come marking and the incision... Ah, I'm getting ahead of myself again.”
“The area you're disinfecting is larger than I expected... I know the operation requires it. I just suddenly feel like there's nowhere for me to hide.”
“Is this the disinfection before the incision...? Wait, I'm still awake and haven't had anesthesia... I'm finding it hard to breathe.”
“So cold... It's only disinfection, but I keep thinking about the blade coming next. Doctor, are you really about to begin...?”
“Please tell me what steps are still left! I know I've asked too much... But if I don't ask, I can't stop thinking about it.”
“Is this where the incision will be...? I understand. Seeing that spot marked just made my heart sink.”
“This mark has to match the surgical plan, right? All right... I've confirmed it, but I still don't dare look down again.”
“You're really going to cut along this line... without any anesthesia at all? I-I know you explained it already, but now I'm so frightened...”
“Wait, let me see it clearly first... No, never mind! I don't actually dare look... Doctor, don't bring the blade over yet!”
“The marking is finished... You won't make the incision immediately, will you? I'm sorry. I've been asking for details all this time, and now I'm afraid to hear the answer.”
Doctor, I meant to finish handing over my work before coming in... But this is what's been happening with my body: {line}
The most noticeable symptom is: {line}. I can explain it again in chronological order so I don't leave anything out.
Please note one more thing as well: {line}. Sorry, I always feel that leaving out even one detail could affect the assessment afterward.

My name is Rami Amasaki. I'm a new member of VTX Union's Special Section 3 and the co-pilot of the prototype Tiranedo. Ever since graduating from military university, I've been used to checking every step repeatedly... But when something goes wrong with my own body, the more I try to understand it, the more nervous I become.
strings.patient_bundles.patient_rami_amasaki.enc: “I-I have to take everything off for the examination...? I understand why it is necessary, but... Could you first tell me what each step will involve? I am not trying to delay things, really!”
“We are leaving this examination for now?... Phew, that is a relief. But if it is necessary, please do not leave it out just because I hesitated.”
“U-understood. I will cooperate. Please just close the curtain first and give me a little time to get ready... Sudden orders make me panic instead.”
“Thank you for explaining it first... Now I can do things in order. Having someone watch while my body is examined is still more embarrassing than I imagined.”
“I-I am sorry... But please do not rush me like that! I will cooperate with the examination. The harsher you are, the harder it is for me to collect my thoughts...”
strings.patient_bundles.patient_rami_amasaki.pre: Rami Amasaki's Preoperative Arrangements
“Dr. Sakaguchi... I have handed over my work at Special Section 3. Could we check today's surgical arrangements once more? I am worried I missed something.”

“I would like to ask about the details... Once I am on the table, in what order will positioning, disinfection, and the incision happen? If I do not understand it beforehand, I am afraid I will keep imagining the worst.”

At first, Rami listens to each explanation as if checking a prototype aircraft's procedural checklist, quietly asking about several steps. But when the medical staff describe the incision, retraction, and actual procedure to come, she finally stops her note-taking-like questions and grips the blanket with both hands. The details meant to reassure her have instead painted what is coming all too clearly.

“All right. I will stop checking everything again... At least this once, I want to trust others to watch over every step for me. Please take care of me...”
Rami Amasaki enters general anesthesia and no longer speaks as an awake patient. The team completes its final checks and begins the selected procedure.

“Has the local anesthesia taken effect? All right... I will stay still. If something feels wrong, I will tell you immediately.”
“You are really starting without anesthesia...? Wait, I know we already confirmed this, but now the thought of that blade is making my mind go blank!”
